Chapter 11: Embracing the Grip of Grace—Living Forward.
You know, there comes a moment when the stories we’ve heard, the lessons we’ve learned, and those quiet, unexpected moments of grace start to shape more than just our beliefs. They begin to shape the way we actually live, day by day. The grip of grace isn’t just this gentle, passive comfort. It’s an open invitation to live with real courage—to risk loving others deeply, and to step into the unknown, holding onto hope.
Picture this: a teacher watching her students wrestle with self-doubt. She sees how quickly they give up when things get tough, how easily they start to believe the worst about themselves. But instead of zeroing in on their mistakes, she chooses a different path. She speaks words of encouragement, reminds them of their worth, and keeps offering second chances. Slowly, her classroom transforms. It becomes a place where students actually feel safe enough to try, to mess up, and to grow. The grip of grace changes more than just their report cards—it changes their lives.
Most of us don’t realize just how much the way we see ourselves shapes the choices we make. If we think love is something we have to earn, we start playing it safe, hiding our flaws, settling for less than we’re capable of. But when we trust that we’re already held in the grip of grace, everything shifts. Suddenly, we’re free to live boldly, to take risks, and to chase after dreams we once thought were impossible.
I think of a man who spent years playing it safe, afraid to chase after what he really wanted. One day, though, he decided to go for his long-held dream—knowing there were no promises, and that failure was a real possibility. But here’s the thing: he also knew his worth wasn’t on the line. The road got tough—there were setbacks, doubts, and moments of wanting to give up. But through it all, he discovered something new: a sense of purpose that came not from fear, but from the steady, unshakable grip of grace.
Living forward, held by grace, means letting go of those old stories—the ones filled with shame, or fear, or that nagging sense of never being enough. It’s about embracing a new story, one rooted in acceptance, hope, and the real possibility of change. And it’s not just for us. It means offering that same grace to others—creating spaces where people can be real, where love always wins out over judgment.
Over time, this way of living just becomes who we are. The grip of grace isn’t only a safety net. It’s a launch pad—a source of strength, courage, and joy. It’s the foundation for a life that’s truly well-lived, a life marked by a love that simply never lets go.
